The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent high-level goal (HLG) of 'Ensure transparent and traceable product sourcing'. Each LLG is directly supported by documentary evidence from the project description. The LLGs accurately represent the system's functionalities, including viewing product origin details, browsing farmer offers, placing orders with minimum quantity constraints, modifying orders due to availability issues using precedence rules and fair-play score, reviewing and accepting modified orders, and cancelling orders when all products are unavailable. No essential capabilities are missing or misrepresented.

The LLGs are non-redundant, each representing a distinct system interaction or effect. They do not duplicate any parent capability, instead breaking down the HLG into manageable, documented interactions. The automatic effects, such as order cancellation upon complete unavailability and fair-play score updates, are correctly identified as documentary automatic effects that do not require manual triggers by the customer actor.

The LLGs align with the actor criterion of document-supported automatic notifications and system operations, without requiring a manual trigger by the customer actor. Responsibility and scope are accurately represented in each LLG, focusing on system interactions rather than UI mechanics.

In conclusion, the current LLGs fully and correctly realize the parent HLG through documented functional interactions or effects, adhering to the specified criteria without any unsupported or misleading elements.
